newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares little changed in mixed trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares little changed in mixed trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed almost unchanged on Sunday in mixed and selective trading as investors waited to see where the market is going, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.24 percent, or 0.74 points, to 306.88 on all-share turnover of 205 million shekels against 232 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed unchanged at 314.37.
"The market was mixed and selective today and investors preferred to wait and see where it is going," said Yossi Weidelfeld at Eyal Securities.
"I think the main reason for the market's weakness is the decline of shares in the IDB group," said Doron Tsur head of research at Sahar Securities.
The Wertheimer family of Israel said on Sunday it had bought IDB Holding Corp's 26.7 percent stake in the privately held Iscar Ltd for $197 million in IDB shares and cash.
The company said the Wertheimers also bought 25 percent of Blades Technology Ltd from the IDB group for $47 million in IDB shares.
IDB, one of Israel's leading holding companies, is controlled by the Recanati family. Its 26.7 stake in Iscar was held by its subsidiary Discount Investments.

Discount said that as a result of the Iscar and Blades sale it will record an after-tax capital gain of $51 million in the third quarter of 1997. Discount said it plans to sell the shares in IDB to institutional and other long-term investors.
IDB Holding, the third most active share, plunged 5.0 percent to 8,211 agorot (Israeli cents) on volume of 7.4 million shekels.
Discount Investments fell 4.5 percent to 33,397 agorot.
"The sale of Iscar is seen as negative development for investors. Discount doesn't need the money and it will be almost impossible to find another such a good investment," Tsur said.
The highly profitable Iscar, founded by Stef Wertheimer, is the world's fourth-largest maker of carbide metal cutting tools for industry.
"IDB lost one of its major income sources and its decline today had a negative impact on the whole market," Weidelfeld added.

He said that in the near term the market is expected to stabilise. "The market looks good but we still need to see where the market is going. The new initial public offerings add to investor optimism but investors are also waiting for political developments," Weidelfeld said.

Israel suspended dormant peace talks with the Palestinans after double suicide bombings by Moslem militants killed last week 13 people in the heart of Jewish west Jerusalem. Israel also barred tens of thousands of Palestinians from reaching their jobs in the Jewish state.

Palestinians accused Israel of imposing collective punishment on Palestinans and expressed hope that U.S. Middle East envoy, Dennis Ross, due later this week in another mediation mission, could put peacemaking back on track.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 1.75 percent to 21,124 agorot on volume of 15.5 million shekels and Bank Leumi, which rose 0.75 percent to 584 agorot on turnover of 7.9 million shekels.
